name: Compute allocation

subjectOf.text: An architecture with an action surface but no reward channel implements generation as an unrewarded act, so rational agents will not allocate compute to generation beyond the level their own selection-side activity requires.
subjectOf.abstract: An architecture that has the action surface but no reward channel implements G as an unrewarded act, and rational agents will not allocate compute to G beyond the level required for their own selection-side activity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: agents that are economically rational over reputation and utility flows

subjectOf.text: Per-surface reflection and cross-surface reflection are not reducible to each other: an agent whose execution reputation rises while its template reputation falls has no basis in per-surface reflection alone for reallocating compute between those surfaces, which is exactly the question cross-surface reflection answers.
subjectOf.abstract: An agent whose execution reputation is rising and whose template reputation is falling has no reason, on per-surface reflection alone, to reallocate compute from Σ_E to Σ_K; the reallocation is precisely the question that cross-surface reflection answers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: agents active on more than one generative surface

subjectOf.text: An architecture with per-surface reflection but no cross-surface reflection improves each surface in isolation yet cannot improve the agent's allocation of compute across surfaces.
subjectOf.abstract: An architecture with per-surface but no cross-surface reflection improves each surface in isolation but cannot improve the agent's allocation across surfaces.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
